title: Binary Number in a Linked List

concept.title: Build the number while you walk
body: The nodes hold the bits of a binary number, **most significant bit first**. You can compute the value in one walk without knowing the length: every new bit shifts the number built so far one place to the left (multiplying by 2) and adds the new bit.

body.code:
value = 0
while head is not None:
    value = value * 2 + head.val
    head = head.next
return value

body: For `1 0 1`: `0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 5`. This "accumulate while traversing" pattern is the basic way to compute anything over a list: a sum, a maximum, a count, or here a number. In C++ and Java use 64-bit integers.

statement: The nodes of a singly linked list hold the bits 0 or 1 of a binary number, most significant bit first. Print the value of the number in decimal.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`, the number of nodes. The second line has the values of the nodes, from the head to the tail.
hints: The first node is the most significant bit.
For every node, double the value so far and add the bit.
Use 64-bit integers; the number can have up to 62 bits.

import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

# Every node is also remembered in this list. Python in the browser cannot free a very long chain of nodes at once,
# so free_nodes() (called at the end) cuts the links first and the nodes are then freed one by one.
all_nodes = []


class ListNode:
    def __init__(self, val, next=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = next
        all_nodes.append(self)


def free_nodes():
    for node in all_nodes:
        node.next = None
        if hasattr(node, "random"):
            node.random = None
    all_nodes.clear()


# Builds a list from the values. If pos is 0 or more, the last node points back to the node at index pos (a cycle).
def build_list(values, pos=-1):
    head = None
    for v in reversed(values):
        head = ListNode(v, head)
    if pos >= 0:
        tail = head
        while tail.next is not None:
            tail = tail.next
        target = head
        for _ in range(pos):
            target = target.next
        tail.next = target
    return head


# Prints the values of a list on one line ("empty" for an empty list).
def print_list(head):
    out = []
    while head is not None:
        out.append(head.val)
        head = head.next
